label: The lifecycle record cannot carry a receipt: the helper validates schemaVersion 2 and evaluate/write_record rebuild and copy only fixed keys, so an extra skill field would be dropped on the next matched turn.
The helper's atomic write (O_EXCL temp, fsync, rename, dir fsync) and exclusive flock are private to its fixed op table; a receipt cannot ride the lock without a new helper op.
Every lifecycle helper call is a python3 spawnSync capped at 750 ms that returns null on any failure, so each extra op the receipt needs costs one process spawn per turn.
Lifecycle state is partitioned by sha256(cwd)[:12] under directive-lifecycle/, so cwd splitting alone does not rule out .skilled/skills/.state/; its repo scoping does.

Vibe head receipts and the lifecycle store share base resolution, one sha256(sessionId)[:16] file per session, oldest-by-mtime eviction at a 64-style cap, and the lifecycle store removes temp files after 5 minutes.

Because a missing or stale receipt makes the guard deliver (today's behavior), a lock-free temp-file-plus-rename store is safe: concurrent writers, eviction races and torn files can only cause a guard miss. Inferred; 011 freezes a two-writer test.

Recommended Q2 design: a pure-TS store in hooks/lib/route-receipt.ts under <state base>/route-receipts/<sha16>.json, wx temp plus renameSync, no lock, bound from MAX_DIRECTIVE_LIFECYCLE_SESSIONS, mtime eviction, 5-minute temp cleanup, symlink refusal and a size cap; the receipt stores the lifecycle clock {storeGeneration, lifecycleEpoch} from state.clock().

A boundary runs advance-session (new epoch token) or advance-generation (new generation token), and the boundary adapter ignores its boundary field, so a clock-bound receipt expires on every boundary that reaches the store; which hosts register the adapter is still unconfirmed.
Pure-TS sibling route-receipts store, temp+rename, no lock, 64 bound
Receipt stores lifecycle clock; boundary rotation expires it
Any receipt failure (missing, unreadable, oversized, wrong version, clock mismatch, null clock) yields delivery exactly as today.
